title: Compatible local deformations of isolated curve singularities lift globally
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $X$ be a proper $k$-scheme [def-weil-proper-morphism] of dimension at most one, and let $p_1,\ldots,p_r$ be distinct closed points such that $X$ is smooth over $k$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] off these points. Put $R_n=k[t]/(t^n)$ for $n\geq1$. For every $i,n$ suppose given a local $R_n$-algebra $C_{i,n}$, flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and essentially of finite type [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra], with isomorphisms $C_{i,n+1}/t^nC_{i,n+1}\cong C_{i,n}$ compatible under iterated reduction, and $C_{i,1}\cong\mathcal O_{X,p_i}$. Then there are proper flat finitely presented schemes $X_n\to\operatorname{Spec}R_n$ [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], an identification $X_1\cong X$, and compatible isomorphisms $X_{n+1}\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R_{n+1}}\operatorname{Spec}R_n\cong X_n$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Under the underlying-space identifications given by these nilpotent closed immersions, there are isomorphisms of local $R_n$-algebras $\mathcal O_{X_n,p_i}\cong C_{i,n}$, compatible with reduction and the prescribed special-fibre identifications. The finite list may be empty.

source.place: Tag 0DZP, lemma-curve-isolated, first smooth arrow; formal-system consequence of Tag 06HN, formal-defos.tex, lemma-smooth-morphism-essentially-surjective, as used in the middle paragraph of Tag 0E7Y. Properness is preserved under the nilpotent deformations of the proper special fibre.

proof.text: Properness makes $X$ separated and of finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Apply [lem-sfb-isolated-curve-two-affine-cover] to $P=\{p_1,\ldots,p_r\}$. Fix $X=U\cup V$ as there: $V$ contains all the prescribed points, $U$ avoids them, and $U$ and $U\cap V$ are smooth affine schemes. This is the fixed cover used at every level; no affine intersection is inferred from quasi-separatedness alone.

source.place: Tag 0DZP, lemma-curve-isolated, first paragraph of the proof.

proof.text: We construct the tower recursively, keeping both the reductions $\theta_n:(X_{n+1})_{R_n}\cong X_n$ and isomorphisms $h_{i,n}:\mathcal O_{X_n,p_i}\cong C_{i,n}$ in the induction data. Start with $X_1=X$ and with $h_{i,1}$ the inverse of the prescribed $C_{i,1}\cong\mathcal O_{X,p_i}$. The scheme $X_1$ is flat over $k$ by [lem-pc-flat-field]. At the inductive stage $R_{n+1}\twoheadrightarrow R_n$ respects the augmentations to $k$, and its kernel is $(t^n)/(t^{n+1})$, whose square is zero since $2n\geq n+1$. Each $R_n$ is finite-dimensional over $k$, has unique maximal ideal $(t)$, and has residue field $k$: an element is invertible exactly when its constant coefficient is nonzero, with inverse given by a finite geometric series.

source.place: Tag 06HN, formal-defos.tex, lemma-smooth-morphism-essentially-surjective, proof: inductive construction of xi_n and compatible arrows.

proof.text:
Suppose the construction has reached $X_n$ with its special fibre identified with $X$. Let $V_n\subseteq X_n$ be the open corresponding to $V$. Its special fibre is $V$, and the closed immersion $V\hookrightarrow V_n$ is a thickening: on affine charts it is reduction modulo $(t)$, and every prime contains the nilpotent element $t$. Thus $V_n$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-thickening-affine-scheme]. For each marked point its local ring is canonically the local ring of $X_n$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization]. Write this identification as $\lambda_{i,n}:\mathcal O_{V_n,p_i}\cong\mathcal O_{X_n,p_i}$. Give $D_i=C_{i,n+1}$ the specified reduction isomorphism
$$D_i\otimes_{R_{n+1}}R_n\cong C_{i,n}\xrightarrow{h_{i,n}^{-1}}\mathcal O_{X_n,p_i}\xrightarrow{\lambda_{i,n}^{-1}}\mathcal O_{V_n,p_i}.$$
All local flatness and essential-finite-type assumptions on $D_i$ are precisely the hypotheses of the item.

source.place: Tag 0DZP, lemma-curve-isolated, final sentence; Tag 0DYX, lemma-affine, proof (affineness of nilpotent deformations).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-affine-isolated-deformation-lift] with $A'=R_{n+1}$, $A=R_n$, the fixed affine $V$, and its affine deformation $V_n$. It gives an affine flat $R_{n+1}$-scheme $Z$, a reduction isomorphism $e:Z_{R_n}\cong V_n$, and local isomorphisms $b_i:\mathcal O_{Z,p_i}\cong C_{i,n+1}$. Their reductions commute with the isomorphisms chosen in the previous step. This use requires smoothness only away from the prescribed points; it does not require those points to be singular, nor does it require complete-intersection singularities.

source.place: Tag 0DZF, lemma-isolated, first arrow, as applied in the final sentence of the proof of Tag 0DZP.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-open-deformation-lift] to $X=U\cup V$, $Y=X_n$, and $Z$ with $e$. Obtain a flat $R_{n+1}$-scheme $X_{n+1}$, an isomorphism $\theta_n:(X_{n+1})_{R_n}\cong X_n$, and $\gamma:(X_{n+1})_V\cong Z$ with $e\circ\gamma_{R_n}=\theta_n|_{V_n}$. Set the special-fibre identification of $X_{n+1}$ to be that of $X_n$ composed with the reduction of $\theta_n$. Since the open $(X_{n+1})_V$ is affine (it is isomorphic to $Z$), [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] identifies its stalks with those of $X_{n+1}$. Compose the local identification induced by $\gamma$ with $b_i$ to define $h_{i,n+1}$. The displayed equation for $\gamma$ and the reduction equation for $b_i$ give exactly
$$\overline{h}_{i,n+1}:\mathcal O_{X_{n+1},p_i}/t^n\xrightarrow{\sim} C_{i,n+1}/t^n\cong C_{i,n},$$
with $\overline{h}_{i,n+1}$ equal to $h_{i,n}$ after the identification induced by $\theta_n$. This checks the compatibility of the chosen local isomorphisms, not just the existence of their isomorphism classes.

source.place: Tag 0DZN, lemma-glueing-smooth, second arrow, as used in Tag 0DZP; compatibility follows the commutative square in the proof of Tag 06HN.

proof.text: For every constructed $X_n$, the special-fibre square over $R_n\twoheadrightarrow k$ is cartesian and the kernel $(t)$ satisfies $(t)^n=0$. Its special-fibre morphism is the given proper $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Apply [lem-sfb-proper-nilpotent-base-change-reflection] with $A=R_n$ and $I=(t)$ to conclude that $X_n\to\operatorname{Spec}R_n$ is proper. Thus the induction has preserved properness without choosing any algebraization or projective embedding.

Each $R_n$ is Noetherian: every ideal is a subspace of the finite-dimensional $k$-vector space with basis $1,t,\ldots,t^{n-1}$, and a finite $k$-basis of that ideal also generates it as an $R_n$-ideal. The one affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}R_n$ is therefore a locally Noetherian scheme by [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Properness implies finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism], in particular locally finite type and quasi-compact. Apply [pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth] to obtain local finite presentation. By [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated] the morphism is also quasi-separated. These three conditions give finite presentation by [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], including at $n=1$.

source.place: Tag 01TX, morphisms.tex, lemma-noetherian-finite-type-finite-presentation; definitions of proper and finite presentation.

proof.text: Choose the extension data at each successor stage and continue the recursion over $n\geq1$. Define every longer reduction by composing the adjacent $\theta_n$ and their base changes. For three levels the two composites agree by associativity of composition and of base change. The adjacent equations for $h_{i,n}$ then give every iterated reduction equation by induction on the difference of the levels. The given local transition maps already satisfy these equations. When $r=0$, the affine lifting statement has no prescribed local factors and the same recursion applies. When $X=\varnothing$, the construction can be the empty scheme at every level. This proves all the clauses of the item.

source.place: Tag 06HN, lemma-smooth-morphism-essentially-surjective, second paragraph of the proof: continuing the compatible induction.
